verdict.rationale: The public zulip/zulip GitHub repository accepts code contributions and contains server files such as zerver/openapi/zulip.yaml, so the source is readable. Its open licensing is supported only by community statements that it is "100% FOSS" and was "open sourced". missing for 10: a first-party statement naming the specific open-source license, and documentation that the whole product (server and clients) is under that license.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: Contributing code. Check out our guide for new contributors to get started.
The zulip/zulip repository ships a complete OpenAPI 3.0.1 description of the API
Zulip is my favorite modern chat program because it's actually 100% FOSS, unlike Mattermost and RocketChat, which are only 'open core'.
Good to see it be open sourced.
